title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). X is smooth projective of dimension n over an algebraically closed field k. A is an abelian variety and Z lies in A^i_alg(X×A). Z gives two objects:
- a map u_Z : A(k) → A^i_alg(X), presumably cycles algebraically equivalent to 0 modulo rational equivalence (otherwise u_Z would be trivially 0);
- an l-adic map a(^tZ) : H^{2(n-i)+1}(X)(n-i) → H^1(A).

The 'Théorème 3.1', marked with '?' and 'dém. pas faite', asks whether u_Z = 0 ⇔ a(^tZ) = 0, modulo torsion / with Q_l coefficients. In other words: is the Chow-theoretic map from an abelian family of cycles detected by its action on H^1?

This page continues the proof strategy.

Step 1 (reduction to a curve). Choose an 'ample curve' f : C → A whose image generates A, so that C(k) generates the group A(k). Pull Z back to Z' = (1×f)^*Z in A^i_alg(X×C).
- Because C(k) generates A(k), u_{Z'} = 0 implies u_Z = 0 (the arrow ⇐ on the first line).
- Because H^1(A) → H^1(C) is injective, a(^tZ) = 0 ⇔ a(^tZ') = 0.
- So it suffices to treat the case A = C.

Step 2 (Künneth splitting). The Künneth decomposition H^N(X×C) = H^N(X)⊗H^0(C) + H^{N-1}(X)⊗H^1(C) + H^{N-2}(X)⊗H^2(C) is algebraic, 'as one easily checks'.
- In modern terms: the curve C has algebraic Künneth projectors π_0 = [c_0×C], π_2 = [C×c_0], π_1 = Δ − π_0 − π_2.
- Tensoring with the identity of X gives algebraic projectors on X×C.
- These act already at the level of Chow groups.

Step 3 (discarding the extreme pieces). Take N = 2i and split Z' = Z'_0 + Z'_1 + Z'_2.
- Z'_0 = pr_X^*(Z'|X×c_0) gives a constant family, so u = 0 and a = 0.
- Z'_2 = (pr_{X*}Z')×c_0 gives u = 0 (after normalising by the base point) and a = 0.
- So one is reduced to a cycle in the middle Künneth component H^{2i-1}(X)⊗H^1(C). Equivalently, its 'restriction' to X×c_0 and its push-forward to X both vanish.

Next page. 'Astuce de Tate sur les cycles décomposables' is the intended next step. Presumably it handles middle-component cycles that are sums of products, i.e. correspondences factoring through Jacobians / H^1.

In modern terms this is the Chow–Künneth decomposition h(C) = h^0 + h^1 + h^2 of a curve, used to reduce the question to correspondences in Hom(h^1(C), h^{2i-1}(X)), which essentially control the algebraic representative / Abel–Jacobi map.
errors: The conjectured equivalence (Theorem 3.1) is false in the direction a(^tZ)=0 ⇒ u_Z=0. Counterexample: X a complex K3 surface (or any surface with p_g>0, q=0), i=n=2, C a curve of positive genus on X, Z' the graph of the embedding. Then H^{2(n-i)+1}(X)=H^1(X)=0, so a(^tZ')=0 automatically, yet C(k) → CH_0(X)_hom is non-constant by Mumford (1969, 'Rational equivalence of 0-cycles on surfaces'). Grothendieck himself flagged the statement with '?' and 'dém. pas faite'. The direction u_Z=0 ⇒ a(^tZ)=0 is plausible (via Bloch–Srinivas type decomposition over a universal domain).

Minor: u_Z=0 ⇐ u_{Z'}=0 needs C(k) to generate A(k) as a group. This holds for an ample/generating curve but is only half-stated (the previous page writes 'C(k) → A(k) surjectif [?]', which is too strong; generation suffices).
The reduction steps on this page (Steps 1–3) are themselves correct.

ideas.what: Reduce a statement about families of cycles parametrized by an abelian variety to families parametrized by a curve, via a generating curve and injectivity of H^1(A)→H^1(C)
ideas.modern_name: Reduction to curves / Lefschetz-type hyperplane argument for abelian varieties

ideas.what: Künneth components of X×C are algebraic, given by projectors pt×C, C×pt, Δ−π0−π2, acting even on Chow groups
ideas.modern_name: Chow–Künneth decomposition of the motive of a curve h(C)=h^0+h^1+h^2
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968) and Kleiman's exposé in Dix exposés; Demazure/Kleiman motive notes

ideas.what: Conjecture that a family of cycles over an abelian variety is trivial in Chow iff its l-adic action H^{2(n-i)+1}(X)(n-i)→H^1(A) vanishes
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity of the algebraic representative / Abel–Jacobi on images of abelian varieties (Murre's algebraic representative; Bloch–Beilinson filtration F^1/F^2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Griffiths, Murre (algebraic representatives, 1983–85); disproved in general by Mumford (1969)

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out a routine reduction (generating curve plus Chow–Künneth for curves) toward a conjecture that Grothendieck flagged as unproved. That conjecture is in fact false in general by Mumford's theorem on 0-cycles. A mildly interesting historical snapshot of Grothendieck testing whether Chow-theoretic families are detected by l-adic H^1, but nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'ayant[?] la décomposition' is probably 'Or la décomposition ...' with 'tout' struck. The sentence reads: 'Or la décomposition H^N(X×C) ≃ ... est algébrique, comme on vérifie aisément.'
The last Künneth term is cut off at the page margin: H^{N-2}(X)⊗H^2(C).
'dont la projection sur X': the word 'projection' is underlined/overwritten in the manuscript, not cleanly struck. The meaning is the push-forward to X.
